scope: Three-reed ecology education across Hays Botany Learner, Field ID and Quiz. Not an audit of all ~1,200 unrelated species.
media_notes: All 29 physically archived source photographs decoded with Pillow in CI and had a declared creator, license and HTTPS source page; file counts and metadata matched.

Five archived Zizaniopsis files: only three dedicated comparison panels and six reviewed arrows. Two other photographs remain anatomy role review pending; source is Florida, not a Kyle or Hays County voucher.
Other study-only externally hosted panel references are not counted as physical archived images and their remote load/permissions are not independently guaranteed.
Four user-supplied R. Neil Reese/SDSU source photographs remain excluded from public GitHub Pages because express public display permission was not confirmed.
The uploaded AoB PLANTS Figure 5 with C. S. Hood photo credit is a science comparison reference; earlier acquisition attempted but failed, never counted as archived.

beginner_lesson.learner: Four actual owned/attributed specimen photo steps for Arundo and Phragmites, then anatomy and taxon-context details; unchanged 13 Phragmites identification lesson tiles and Arundo's six.
beginner_lesson.field_id: Fix simple five-step crew guide priority; compare three reed-like plants with side-by-side credited habit, optional actual archived collar and flowering photos, and source-specific cautions.
beginner_lesson.glossary: Term explanations retained. Basic labels use plain-English introductions, specialist morphology is expandable.
beginner_lesson.safety: Phragmites species recognition does not infer native or Eurasian introduced lineage from a photo; remain unresolved where needed.

advanced_lesson.arundo: Source-derived character descriptions for clasping blade-base shoulders, measured ligule, spikelet, paired glumes, hairy lemma versus largely non-silky rachilla; decisive same-specimen hair origin macro remains missing.
advanced_lesson.phragmites: Native americanus, introduced Eurasian australis, and Gulf Coast berlandieri distinctions; peer-reviewed genetics-grouped mean ± SE/n for ligule and glumes shown with non-diagnostic overlap warning; Gulf true inner ligule and lineage-verified glumes not pictured.
advanced_lesson.zizaniopsis: Sex-separated spikelets and long true membranous ligule are described via morphology literature, not claimed proven by current macro photos. Sex position conflict across source treatments preserved.

quiz.reed_challenge: Ten source-linked photo/anatomy questions, 4 options each, credited, with feedback, links to source photo and exact Field ID, score and accurate replay label. This remains educational assessment, not expert certification.
quiz.audit: tests/test_reed_quiz.cjs PASS, all 10 image paths/answer IDs/credits and 3 species required.

code_quality.tests: 3 existing Python learner integrity, 4 new Python closeout integrity, 4 JS syntax checks and 10-question Node test ALL PASS
code_quality.browser_limitation: No live click-through/mobile visual confirmation was performed in this audit; latest GitHub Pages deployment can confirm build success but not subjective visual alignment on user device.

remaining_photo_requirements: Phragmites: voucher/genetically associated Gulf berlandieri opened true inner ligule with mm scale and genuine separate mature glumes; existing outer-sheath and whole panicle references DO NOT substitute
Arundo: paired same-specimen rachilla/lemma hair origin 10-20x with ruler; already has readable diagnostic collage and separated spikelets, but not decisive paired hair-origin macro
Zizaniopsis: opened long 6–20 mm ligule, leaf-margin serrations, and same-branch anther/stigma verified male/female spikelets with mm scale; don't infer sex from position alone
Independent live-mobile arrow-overlay check on all displayed starter photo panels remains a useful user field review.
decision: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS retained for Phragmites/Arundo/Zizaniopsis. Strong crew field learner and defensible expert research caveats, but no justified all-photos-or-genetic-100% claim.
